# An all-active-menu obstruction to exposed targets and full own-cone isolation

This is an actual positive-width mixed convex example with a unique deepest
source. EVERY balanced active menu fails the common exposed-base interior
target criterion. Moreover every response atom is smaller than Gamma_2,
and the entire own-source projective cone cannot be isolated by convex
physical fields. The example is well above OC and does not obstruct
selective free-facet payment or a more general best-menu theorem.

The target criterion audited here is Section1 of
`candidate 80791dd8739dad42`.
Its sufficient payment proof is not challenged.

## 1. A concrete actual compatible family and smoothing scale

Let n=1,d=2, and write

    A=(2,-1), B=(-1,2), C=(-1,-1), T=conv{A,B,C},
    V=|T|=9/2, sigma=1/100,
    D_sigma=(1-sigma)A+sigma T, v=|D_sigma|=V sigma^2=9/20000.

Use complete integer base {-1,0,1} and fibers

    K_0=T,    K_-1=K_1=D_sigma.

They are the ACTUAL integer fibers of their canonical convex hull: the
two endpoint fibers agree and lie in T, so the middle fiber is exactly T.
The endpoint centers are (1-sigma)A while the middle center is0, so the
fiber centers are not the restriction of an affine graph.

Use the buffer-free outward uniform kernel, with any

    0<h<=1/100000.

The pooled covariance and continuous norm are exactly

    Sigma=t_sigma Sigma_T,
    t_sigma=(1+2sigma^4)/(1+2sigma^2)<=1,
    Sigma_T=[[1/2,-1/4],[-1/4,1/2]],
    Gamma(u)=sqrt(u^T Sigma u).

This is within-fiber covariance, so the nonaffine translations introduce
no extra between-fiber term. Its largest eigenvalue is at most3/4.
The physical strip width in unit continuous direction is at most
h sqrt(3)/2. Since diam(T)=3sqrt(2), smoothing changes a T cap by less
than4h. Put

    delta=v+4h<=49/100000.                            (1)

## 2. The unique deepest source is in the middle and near0

For any own direction at base0, a sufficiently large finite base tilt
saturates one endpoint fiber and empties the other. Thus mixed depth at
any middle mark y is at most its ordinary T depth plus delta. The ordinary
maximum depth of T is2, attained at0; therefore the mixed maximal raw
smoothed depth Q satisfies

    2<=Q<=2+delta.                                   (2)

The lower bound follows by using middle mark0: every nonvertical mixed
cap contains at least its ordinary through-centroid T cap of area2;
pure-base caps are larger. At an endpoint base, isolate that exposed fiber
by finite base tilt. Its maximal depth is at most

    2sigma^2+4sigma h<2.

Hence every deepest source is in the middle fiber.

For a deepest mark y=(y1,y2), its ordinary T depth is at least2-delta.
The three canonical directions e1,e2,-e1-e2 give T cap areas
V(2-u.y)^2/9. Consequently

    u.y<=a_delta:=2-sqrt(4-2delta)<=delta

for all three directions. Since their sum is0,

    |y1|,|y2|<=2delta.                               (3)

In particular y has a fixed own inball, all small-width own strips are
proper, and no pure-base cap is active (its mass is at least V+v).
Finite clipping gives attained active normals. Cap C1 differentiation
and positive threshold coarea give m_eff/S=Y. If two middle marks were
deepest, an active cap at their midpoint would propagate to both endpoints
by the linear depth-superlevel inequalities, and this same identity would
force them equal. This is the buffer-free singleton proof from the earlier
smoothing note, and proves a UNIQUE actual deepest mark Y=(0,y).

## 3. ALL active directions lie in three explicit small cones

For any nonzero direction u, rescale it so max{u.A,u.B,u.C}=2. Its three
vertex values sum0. Label the maximizing vertex and write the other two
values as -1+s,-1-s, with |s|<=3. If |s|<=1, the ordinary cap at0 isolates
the maximizing vertex and has area

    18/(9-s^2).

If |s|>=1 it contains two vertices and has area at least V/2=9/4. For the
latter assertion its complementary vertex cap has area fraction
(|s|+1)^2/[2|s|(|s|+3)]<=1/2.

Thus outside the three cones |s|<1/4 the ordinary centroid cap area is at
least

    2+gamma,       gamma=2/143.                       (4)

Moving the mark by (3) changes any ordinary T cap area by at most
diam(T)|y|<=12delta. Smoothing and endpoint contributions are nonnegative.
An active cap outside the three cones would therefore have mass at least
2+gamma-12delta, contradicting (2), because

    13delta<=637/100000<2/143.

The three possible active-direction cones have explicit representatives

    U_A(s)=(1+s/3,2s/3),
    U_B(s)=(2s/3,1+s/3),
    U_C(s)=(-1+s/3,-1-s/3),        |s|<1/4.            (5)

Every active normal, with ANY base tilt, has its continuous direction in
one of these cones. This certifies the full active family, rather than a
chosen symmetric circuit.

## 4. Exact outside costs and failure of EVERY exposed-target menu

For u in U_B or U_C, the endpoint fiber satisfies

    max_(x in D_sigma) u.(x-y)
       <=-(3/4)(1-sigma)+2sigma+4delta<-7/10.

Since h Gamma(u) is much smaller than7/10, base tilt a=0 makes BOTH
endpoint smoothed masses identically zero. For any ACTUALLY active cap
in these two cones, its outside contribution must therefore also be zero:
the fixed-direction zero-outside competitor has the same own cap mass.
All its positive halfspaces exclude every interior point of BOTH endpoint
fibers. Indeed a positive physical margin has kernel value1 on an open
set, which would give strictly positive outside capture.

For u in U_A,

    min_(x in D_sigma) u.(x-y)
       >=2(1-sigma)-(5/4)sigma-4delta>19/10.

For every base tilt a, one endpoint has base margin +|a|, and its entire
fiber is captured. Hence the least possible outside contribution is v,
achieved by finite saturation of exactly one endpoint. ANY active cap in
U_A has outside mass exactly v: one endpoint is fully captured and the
other has zero smoothed capture.

All endpoint smooth coareas are thus ZERO for ALL actual active caps.
Only the middle proper strip contributes to S and the response vector.

Every positively balanced menu uses all three cones. Any two cones lie
in a common open continuous halfspace: use the vectors (1,1) for A/B,
(1,-2) for A/C, and (-2,1) for B/C. Their dot products with (5) are at
least3/4. Thus a balance cannot be supported on only one or two cones.

In particular every balanced active menu includes a B-cone and a C-cone
cap. EACH such cap excludes both endpoint interiors. The only exposed
vertices of the COMPLETE base hull are -1 and1. Therefore no balanced
active menu has a common interior target point on ANY exposed complete-
base fiber. This conclusion covers every active tilt and every circuit.

## 5. Every response atom is also smaller than Gamma_2

For u in (5) retain its scale max vertex value2 and put g=Gamma(u).
The own smoothing strip has levels from u.y-hg to u.y. Throughout it the
cap isolates the same triangle vertex. Direct differentiation of its
area gives the response vector exactly

    S_normalized u_normalized = k_u u,
    k_u=9(2-u.y+hg/2)/(9-s^2).                        (6)

There is no endpoint contribution by Section4. From (1),(3),(5),

    19/10 < k_u < 21/10.                              (7)

Let nu be ANY balanced response menu. Fix a cone, say U_A, and test its
balance against vertex A. Every vector in that cone has u.A=2, while
the other two cones have u.A>=-5/4. Therefore its TOTAL response weight
q_A satisfies

    (19/5)q_A <=(21/8)(1-q_A),
    q_A<=105/257<4/9=Gamma_2.                         (8)

The same argument applies to B and C. Each atom is bounded by its cone's
total weight, so no active response menu has a large paying atom. Every
minimal positive circuit has rank2 and three atoms, never an antipodal
rank1 pair.

The pure-base saturation baseline at the middle is B_0=v. Every A-cone
active cap has deficit0 and every B/C cap has deficit v. Thus no balanced
menu is supported on zero deficit. There is even a uniform quantitative
bound: Gamma(U_j(s))=sqrt(t_sigma/2)*sqrt(1+s^2/3), so its ratio over all
three cones is at most sqrt(49/48). Converting a quantile balance to the
representatives (5) and testing against A gives at least8/13 weight in
B/C. Converting back proves the deficit bound

    D_0 >= (8/13)sqrt(48/49) v > v/2.                 (9)

This is a concrete positive-deficit instance, not merely an abstract
alternative defined by compactness.

## 6. Full own-source projective-cone isolation is impossible as well

The endpoint triangle shares positive-length patches with two middle
facets: the bottom edge y2=-1 and the diagonal edge y1+y2=1, both adjacent
to A. At every point x in either shared patch, the points (-1,x),(1,x),
and their midpoint (0,x) have the SAME corresponding fiber outer normal.

Suppose a nonnegative convex physical field, for that fixed normal,
vanished on both endpoint normal bundles and agreed on the middle fiber
with its entire projective cone field centered at y. Convexity gives

    Phi(n,0,x)<= [Phi(n,-1,x)+Phi(n,1,x)]/2=0

on each shared patch. But the own-source cone field
[h_T(n)-n.y]P_y(x)^(-2) is strictly positive there, since y is interior and
P_y>0. Contradiction. The argument is on positive-length boundary patches,
so it rules out equality almost everywhere as well: continuity of the
finite convex field makes endpoint vanishing extend over each patch.

This eliminates FULL own-source cone isolation, including the strict
support-gap hypothesis. It does not eliminate admissible fields supported
on the free part of those facets or on the third facet. Such selective
free-facet payment is an appropriate remaining mechanism.

## 7. Scope

This actual example simultaneously defeats three sufficient universal
claims: every source has a common exposed-base target, every source has a
large response atom, or its full own projective cone can always be isolated.
It also has strictly positive full-menu saturation deficit. Its normalized
depth is close to4/9, far ABOVE the n=1,d=2 OC target2/9. Hence it is neither
an OC counterexample nor a counterexample to an argument that uses the
additional stationary bad-body separator or selective own-facet credit.

the contributor supplied, and the independent companion
`candidate 05d41ace8d693538`
checks, an actual selective payment for THIS family: its entire facet
opposite A is isolatable, and its limiting weighted profile has efficiency
4t^2/(6t-1)>Gamma_2, with t=(1+sqrt(1-3sigma^2))/6. The strict payment
persists for sufficiently small positive h at fixed sigma. Thus the three
failed sufficient criteria in this note do not exhaust available actual
paying fields, even on this example.
